reviewed_by: Claude Code; root cause independently validated by a fresh subagent (code-troubleshooting skill)
reason: Live Core: Codex command approvals stayed pending after a restart interrupted their turns (pending cards were retired only through in-memory waiters). Approving them days later recorded a delivery intent that record_delivery('failed') turned into adapter_status 'unknown', although no waiter existed and nothing was sent; the handoff inventory then pinned the project on every deploy. Fix: a decision on an ended harness turn expires the card and answers 410; restart and shutdown expire the pending approvals of turns they interrupt; a decision with no waiter records adapter_status 'failed' (not sent) while a completed waiter keeps 'unknown'. Also (operator request) new projects default to approval policy never, and an automation-policy update that omits approval_policy keeps the current value instead of resetting it to on_boundary. Selected: test_stale_harness_approvals.py (new regressions: 3 fail on origin/main, plus the crash-safe unknown guard), test_approval_handoff.py (adapter handoff, unknown resolution, restart reconciliation), test_automation_runtime.py and test_one_browser_cutover.py (policy default; on_boundary tests now opt in explicitly), test_never_policy.py (never semantics).
exclusions: test_approval_continuation.py has a failure (test_cancelled_waiter_does_not_resurrect_terminal_turn) and a hang (test_resolving_one_request_keeps_the_other_pending) identical on origin/main; its other 6 tests pass. test_runtime_orphan_recovery.py (110 passed) and test_handoff_participants.py (20 passed) pass locally but are left out to keep the python job under CI's 300 s limit; neither owns changed code. Locally 4 test_automation_runtime.py tests fail identically on origin/main because this host has a prepared Kali runtime and memory enforcement. Docs: AUTOMATION-RUNTIME.md and the settings-assistant design note state the new default; the product-knowledge index was regenerated and verified. tests/v3/test_automation_runtime.py is not selected: CI has no Nebula memory runner or Kali runtime, so its host-command tests fail there regardless (9 such failures in the first CI run). Locally, with the change, it ran 85 passed plus 4 failures identical on origin/main; its three on_boundary tests now opt into that policy explicitly.
